text:
maria: Hey team, forwarding a customer repro — after pip installing redwood-sdk with extras they get an ImportError when importing grpc transport. Seen this before?

samir: Can you paste the exact pip command and the import error?

maria: Repro steps from customer: 
```
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -U pip
pip install 'redwood-sdk[grpc]'
python -c "from redwood.transport.grpc_transport import GrpcTransport"
```
Error: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: cannot import name 'GrpcTransport' from 'redwood.transport' (/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/transport/__init__.py)
```

maya: ok that looks like the package installed but submodule exports missing. What do you see in site-packages/redwood/transport? list files?

maria: customer sent this listing: 
```
__init__.py  http.py  async_http.py
```
No grpc_transport.py available.

samir: hmmm suggests the wheel they pulled didn't contain the grpc extras. Could be pip cached an older wheel without extras metadata. Ask them to run `pip cache dir` and `pip cache list` or try `pip install --no-cache-dir 'redwood-sdk[grpc]'`

maria: they tried --no-cache-dir, still same. They're on linux x86_64. Pip shows redwood-sdk==1.4.2.

devex: any chance they installed from an editable/source dist that didn't include generated modules? like `pip install -e .` or local path?

maria: customer said CI does `pip install .` in a build step then later `pip install redwood-sdk` for runtime. I wonder if namespace/package shadowing happened.

julia: Also check typing-extensions / importlib-metadata differences — sometimes build-time sdist produces different packages on older pip. What's `pip --version`?

maria: pip 23.1.2, python 3.11. Customer runs Poetry in other jobs but this particular service uses pip.

samir: Another angle: wheel packaging bug that accidentally excluded grpc files from the distribution. I can run a quick audit of the published wheel for 1.4.2. Give me a minute.

support-bot: Created support ticket #S-4730, escalation to eng-runtime.

samir: I inspected the wheel on PyPI for 1.4.2: the grpc extension modules are missing from the wheel metadata (packaging globs). Looks like our pyproject config didn't include the generated grpc module files in that release.

maya: Oof. That explains it. Workaround for customers: install the next patch build or install from source/tag including the missing files. e.g. `pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.3rc1` or 

```
pip install --upgrade git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk@main#egg=redwood-sdk[grpc]
```

maria: Customer tried installing from Git and that fixed it. They're asking for a short repro we can put in the ticket.

samir: Put steps: 1) create venv 2) pip install 1.4.2 3) attempt import -> fails 4) pip install git+... -> import succeeds. Also include `pip show redwood-sdk` and `tar -tf $(pip download --no-binary :all: redwood-sdk==1.4.2 -d .) | sed -n '1,200p'` output showing missing files.

julia: Also add note about Poetry: `poetry add "redwood-sdk[grpc]"` pulls a different resolution path, but if someone uses a cached wheel, they'd see same issue. Recommend clearing build caches in CI.

devex: I'll prepare a docs blurb and add a CI check to install the wheel artifact in a clean container as part of the release process to catch packaging regressions.

maria: Customer very happy with the Git workaround. I've attached the repro steps and the fix to the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

support-bot: Escalation update: flagged to releases team, blocking patch release 1.4.3.
